paras: The killing of Mack Henry was the fatal shooting of a Black man by an unknown assailant near Ichetuchnee, Florida, on Friday, July 27, 1888. The only known report, from the Lake City correspondent of the Savannah Morning News, noted that Henry's wife had been shot and killed at the same place about three months earlier.

In a letter datelined Lake City on July 30, the correspondent wrote that Mack Henry, identified as "colored," had been "shot and killed by some unknown assassin near Ichetuchnee Friday." The same paragraph recalled that "only about three months ago" his wife had been shot and killed "at the same place in the same clandestine manner." The report named no suspect and gave no motive for either killing.

According to the correspondent, "efforts are being made to apprehend the guilty party," though the item did not say who was making them. No report of an arrest, inquest or trial appears in the coverage, and no account of the wife's earlier killing was found.

The Savannah Morning News carried the killing on July 31, 1888, as a three-sentence paragraph at the end of a Lake City letter headed "Lake City as a Critic," which was otherwise devoted to the trustees' demand for Dr. Kost's resignation from the state experiment station and a new principal for the Peabody high school. The item had no headline of its own and offered no comment beyond calling the killings "clandestine." No other newspaper report of the killing was found.

accounts.label: Lake City correspondent
accounts.gist: Mack Henry, colored, was shot dead near Ichetuchnee on Friday by an unknown assassin, at the place where his wife had been killed the same way about three months before; efforts were under way to catch the killer.

framing.detail: Reported as a brief crime item ('some unknown assassin', 'clandestine manner') appended to a Lake City letter headed 'LAKE CITY AS A CRITIC.', with no motive or comment.
